explanations.explanation: There it is, baker! In Isaiah 55:1 the LORD says, "Come, buy wine and milk without money and without cost!" Without money AND without cost. He says it twice so nobody walks up to the counter still digging for a wallet.

I like where your head's at, friend, because nobody likes waiting in line. But in Isaiah 55:1 the LORD says, "Come, buy wine and milk without money and without cost!" He's stacking up how free this is. Free, free, and then FREE again, just in case you missed it the first two times.

Ooh, "without end" has a nice ring to it, I'll give you that. But in Isaiah 55:1 the LORD says, "Come, buy wine and milk without money and without cost!" The point here is the price tag, and there isn't one. If I ran my bakery like that, my cash register would get lonely.

Yes, baker! Right after asking why they spend money on what is not bread, the LORD says in Isaiah 55:2, "Listen carefully to Me, and eat what is good, and your soul will delight in the richest of foods." Quit chasing what leaves you empty and come listen. It's like scrolling for an hour looking for something good when the good thing was sitting right there the whole time.

I see why you'd hesitate, friend, but this one's true. Right after asking why they labor on what does not satisfy, the LORD says in Isaiah 55:2, "Listen carefully to Me, and eat what is good, and your soul will delight in the richest of foods." The fix for empty isn't trying harder. It's listening to Him.

You nailed it, baker! In Isaiah 55:3 the LORD ties the everlasting covenant to "My loving devotion promised to David." And He keeps going about him in verse 4: "Behold, I have made him a witness to the nations, a leader and commander of the peoples." When God puts loving devotion on a promise with your name on it, friend, that's a box nobody's unsealing.

Moses is a strong guess, friend, but he doesn't show up in this passage. In Isaiah 55:3 the LORD calls it "My loving devotion promised to David." David's the man named here. Moses will have to sit in the back for this one, and trust me, I know all about sitting in the back.

Abraham is a solid guess, friend, but this promise has a different name on it. In Isaiah 55:3 the LORD promises an everlasting covenant, and He ties it to "My loving devotion promised to David." Then verse 4 keeps the spotlight on David. Right card, different name tag.

Right on, baker! In Isaiah 55:4 the LORD says, "Behold, I have made him a witness to the nations, a leader and commander of the peoples." Witness, leader, AND commander. Three titles! Meanwhile my title is "guy who packs boxes with his face."

Easy to miss, friend, because the witness part comes first. But in Isaiah 55:4 the LORD keeps going: "a leader and commander of the peoples." So David gets the whole set, witness, leader and commander. That is a LOT of name tags for one shirt.

explanations.answer: Their God has made them glorious
explanations.explanation: Yes, baker! The LORD gives the reason in Isaiah 55:5: "For the LORD your God, the Holy One of Israel, has bestowed glory on you." Look at that word "bestowed." The glory is a gift from God, and it's what gets whole nations RUNNING. I don't run for anything but the oven timer, so that's saying something.

explanations.answer: Their armies have made them strong
explanations.explanation: I can see the logic, friend, since a strong army gets noticed. But the LORD says in Isaiah 55:5 it's because "the LORD your God, the Holy One of Israel, has bestowed glory on you." There's nothing about armies here. God's glory on them is what brings the nations running.

explanations.answer: Their trade has made them rich
explanations.explanation: Money talks, I know, but not in this verse, friend. The LORD says in Isaiah 55:5 the reason is that "the LORD your God, the Holy One of Israel, has bestowed glory on you." And remember, this whole chapter opened with buying "without money and without cost!" Riches aren't the draw here. God's glory is.

That's it, baker! Isaiah 55:7 says to return to the LORD, "that He may have compassion, and to our God, for He will freely pardon." FREELY, friend. No fine print. No processing fee. No "please hold, your pardon is important to us."

I get it, friend, it almost sounds too good to be true. But Isaiah 55:7 says it plainly: "for He will freely pardon." The wicked man forsakes his way, returns to the LORD, and finds compassion waiting. Believe me, an old stamper who spent years behind the takeout menus knows how good it feels when somebody reaches in for you.

Higher, baker! In Isaiah 55:9 the LORD says, "For as the heavens are higher than the earth, so My ways are higher than your ways and My thoughts than your thoughts." Think about how far the sky is above your head. That's the gap. Me, I can barely reach the top shelf over my ovens.

Older sounds wise, friend, but the picture here is about height. In Isaiah 55:9 the LORD says, "For as the heavens are higher than the earth, so My ways are higher than your ways and My thoughts than your thoughts." Heavens up top, earth down below. Look up, way up, and you've got it.

Ha! Simpler would be nice, wouldn't it? But in Isaiah 55:9 the LORD says His ways and thoughts are higher than theirs, just as the heavens are higher than the earth. Higher, friend, WAY up there. Good thing, too, because I once spent twenty minutes looking for the spatula I was holding with my own mustache.

You got it, baker! The LORD finishes the picture in Isaiah 55:11: "so My word that proceeds from My mouth will not return to Me empty, but it will accomplish what I please, and it will prosper where I send it." Rain comes down, the earth buds and sprouts, and the job gets done. His word works just like that.

That's a tender guess, friend, but tears don't show up in this passage. In Isaiah 55:11 the LORD says the word from His mouth won't come back to Him empty. The rain waters the earth, and His word does what He sends it to do. Every drop counts.

So close, friend, because rain and fields really do go together! But the thing being compared comes in Isaiah 55:11, where the LORD says the word that proceeds from His mouth will not return to Him empty. The rain is the picture. His word is the point.

Other way around, friend! In Isaiah 55:11 the LORD says His word "will not return to Me empty, but it will accomplish what I please, and it will prosper where I send it." Empty is the one thing it will NOT do. Me, I send a batch into the oven and sometimes it comes back as charcoal. His word? Never.

Exactly, baker! In Isaiah 55:11 the LORD says His word "will not return to Me empty, but it will accomplish what I please, and it will prosper where I send it." Not empty. Not halfway. It does the job every time. I wish my first thousand cookie stamps had that kind of track record.

YES, baker! In Isaiah 55:12 the LORD says, "You will indeed go out with joy and be led forth in peace; the mountains and hills will burst into song before you, and all the trees of the field will clap their hands." Mountains. Singing. I can't carry a tune past the mixing bowl, and here come the HILLS harmonizing.

Not this time, friend! This is a joyful parade. In Isaiah 55:12 the LORD says they will go out with joy and be led forth in peace, and the mountains and hills will "burst into song" before them. No shaking here, just a hillside choir.

Melting is a cookie problem, friend, not a mountain problem, at least not here. In Isaiah 55:12 the LORD says the mountains and hills will "burst into song" as they go out with joy. This whole scene is joy and peace. Let's leave the melting to my chocolate chips.

Flip it, friend! In Isaiah 55:13 the LORD says that instead of the thornbush, the cypress will grow, and instead of the brier, the myrtle will spring up. The thorns are on their way OUT. It's like tossing a burnt batch and pulling a perfect one out of the oven.

Right you are, baker! In Isaiah 55:13 the thornbush and the brier get replaced. The cypress grows where the thornbush was, and the myrtle springs up where the brier was. Out with the prickly stuff, in with the good trees. Honestly, that's the most satisfying swap since my crooked stamps finally came out straight.

Everlasting, baker! In Isaiah 55:13 the LORD says, "this will make a name for the LORD, an everlasting sign, never to be destroyed." Never to be destroyed, friend. That's a sign that outlasts everything, including whatever I stamped on my first cookie.

Oh, this one goes the long way, friend! In Isaiah 55:13 the LORD calls it "an everlasting sign, never to be destroyed." Temporary is a plate of my cookies sitting in front of me. This sign lasts forever.

Hidden? Not this sign, friend! In Isaiah 55:13 the LORD says it "will make a name for the LORD, an everlasting sign, never to be destroyed." Cypress and myrtle growing right where the thornbush and brier used to be. That's not a secret. That's a sign.
